title: Talk about something on the page and the assistants find it

chat.text: Push-to-talk gets a second mode: Ctrl+Shift+M toggles an open mic; the floating mic shows only while the microphone is live. Queued after it: when you describe something on the page, each utterance carries a compact list of what's visible (headings and items, each with an address, a few hundred tokens, never the raw log); the fast assistant names the element, the smart one answers the same question without seeing that answer, and if they agree the element is highlighted. The blind check becomes a general rule for the pair. Brief: /framework/ai/2026-10-03/point-at-it/

add.title: Or just point: Ctrl+Shift+click
add.text:
- **Hold Ctrl+Shift and click anything** to select it for the AI. Plain clicks stay normal; Escape clears.
- **It selects the meaningful thing first:** clicking the icon inside an icon item selects the whole item; a drill-down mode reaches its children.
- **A small popover** shows what you picked (its icon and name, or just "div") and its tree: parents above, children below, each clickable.
- **The address is exact:** an item's id when it has one, otherwise its position plus the moment it was taken ("as of 4:52 pm"), so nothing has to guess. Your next words carry the selection, so "fix this" needs no matching at all.
- **Built on what exists:** the drawer's inspect-mode selection and the old "pick an element" tool.
